title: A research institution finds one voice for its findings
summary: SAMPLE. A policy research body held strong evidence that decision-makers rarely acted on. The work reframed the findings around the questions its audiences were already asking.
challenge: The institution produced rigorous reports. Readers outside the field found them hard to place and harder to use. Teams inside described the same findings in different ways.
approach: We began by listening to researchers and to the people who receive their work. We interpreted where meaning was lost, then shaped a shared structure for presenting findings: the question, the evidence, the implication.
outcome: The institution now introduces its work in a consistent way, and its reports open with the decision they inform. Staff report that conversations with partners start from a shared understanding.

title: An organisation in transition keeps its stakeholders steady
summary: SAMPLE. During a leadership change, an organisation needed one clear account of what was changing and what was not.
challenge: Partners, staff and funders were each hearing a different version of the transition. Silence from the centre was being read as uncertainty.
approach: We worked with the executive team in confidence to separate what was decided from what was open. We built a short narrative and a sequence for sharing it with each audience.
outcome: Messages to staff, partners and funders now share the same core account. Leaders have a plain way to answer the hardest questions.

title: A growing company clarifies how it wants to be understood
summary: SAMPLE. A founder-led company had outgrown the way it described itself. Customers and investors were reading different stories.
challenge: The company's identity had changed faster than its language. Internally the team agreed on where it was heading. Externally, the picture was less clear.
approach: We interviewed customers and partners, compared their interpretation with leadership intent, and named the gaps. We then shaped positioning that the whole team could explain in the same terms.
outcome: Leadership, sales and investor materials now describe the company in consistent terms, and the team can say why it exists in a sentence.
